final_candidates.decision_summary: Q54R lies just downstream of the RKKRRQRRR core; introducing arginine extends the basic character of the TAR-binding region. MSA and PLM evidence are weakly favorable (z=0.022, z=0.004) with good applicability.

K41R is a charge-conservative K-to-R swap inside the arginine-rich motif; arginine side chains engage TAR RNA more strongly via bidentate contacts. Highest MSA z-score (0.151) among candidates supports viability.
R53K retains positive charge in the core but slightly reduces arginine content; MSA/PLM support is moderate (z=0.064, z=0.043). Kept as the third pick over Y47F and K71R due to core proximity.

stop_reason.detail: All applicable evidence tools have been exhausted on the candidate pool and no phenotype predictor exists, so further rounds would not change the final Top-3.

history.rationale: Position 54 sits in the arginine-rich basic/RNA-binding domain; introducing an additional arginine strengthens TAR RNA binding, which correlates with higher transactivation and replication.
Position 54 lies in the core transactivation domain where basic/polar residues support TAR RNA binding; retained pending evidence.
Moderate MSA frequency of R at 54 and best-in-pool ESM-1v plausibility; position 54 lies in the flexible activation domain where R may enhance TAR RNA contacts. Retained at rank 1.
Conserved basic-patch substitution adjacent to the RKKRR core; MSA and PLM both weakly favorable. Retain top rank.
Position 38 lies in the core transactivation domain; aromatic substitution maintains hydrophobic packing while potentially improving P-TEFb/CycT1 interface contacts.
Aromatic-conservative substitution in the cysteine-rich region; retained pending functional annotation of disulfide/structural constraints.
Zero MSA frequency for W at 38 and near-zero PLM plausibility despite good coverage; evidence argues against natural tolerance.
Core hydrophobic substitution with no evidence of transactivation benefit; slight downgrade.
Position 47 is in the core–basic domain junction; Tyr47 is solvent-exposed in Tat–CycT1 structures and Phe is tolerated, a conservative change near the ARM that may fine-tune TAR interaction.
Conservative aromatic swap near the core domain boundary; low risk to viability.
Conservative aromatic substitution but no homolog support; downgraded below the charge-preserving core-domain candidates.
Conservative aromatic substitution in the core; evidence neutral. Keep as backup.
A conserved-basic-region lysine; Arg substitution can modestly increase electrostatic interaction with TAR RNA and host factors involved in transactivation.
Conservative basic-residue substitution in the glutamine-rich region; retained pending MSA/PLM evidence.
Position 71 is highly conserved (entropy 0.383) with zero MSA support; likely disrupts the RGD motif or flanking function.
Basic-residue swap in C-terminal regulatory region; low impact expected.
Conservative basic-domain substitution; lysine at this position retains RNA binding while occasionally improving flexibility of the ARM for TAR recognition.
Conservative basic substitution in the RGDPTGPKE tail; retained pending evidence.
Second-highest MSA frequency (0.064) and best ESM-1v plausibility (0.043), a conservative charge-preserving swap in the activation domain.
Charge-conservative but R->K slightly reduces arginine content in the RKKRR motif; moderate support only.
Position 41 borders the core domain; Arg may add favorable charge at the TAR-binding interface while preserving overall fold of the transactivation domain.
Conservative basic substitution adjacent to the core domain; viability-preserving.
Highest MSA mutant frequency (0.15) among all candidates at a core domain position, suggesting strong natural tolerance; K→R preserves positive charge in the RGD-adjacent basic region.
K-to-R in the arginine-rich TAR-binding region preserves positive charge with modest MSA/PLM support. Retain.
Position 13 near the acidic/proline N-terminal region; Tyr substitution is seen in some functional Tat variants and may alter host-factor binding favorably.
Weakly supported; retained for re-evaluation with functional annotation on the N-terminal region.
Full MSA coverage but low mutant frequency and very low PLM score; demoted to bottom of pool.
Fully covered position shows near-zero evolutionary tolerance despite applicability 1.0; risky for viability with no clear phenotype gain.
